simple.meaning: גֶּזַע (gezaʻ) is a Hebrew word meaning “the trunk or stump of a tree (as felled or as planted).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: גֶּזַע (H1503) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Job 14:8, with occurrences in Job, Isaiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גֶּזַע (H1503) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in גֶּזַע (H1503) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: גֶּזַע (gezaʻ) / H1503 is traced through Job 14:8, Isaiah 11:1, Isaiah 40:24 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: the trunk or stump of a tree (as felled or as planted)
definitions.full: H1503. geza [ גֶּ֫זַע ] noun masculine Job 14:8 stock, stem (Late Hebrew id. , compare Syriac stem, trunk ) — construct גֶּזַע Isa 11:1 ; suffix גִּזְעוֺ Job 14:8 , גִּזְעָם Isa 40:24 ; — stock, stem of a tree Job 14:8 (|| שֹׁרֶשׁ ); figurative ׳ג ישׁי ' stem of Jesse Isa 11:1 (|| שֹׁרֶשׁ ); ג בָּאָרֶץ ׳שֹׁרֵשׁ 40:24 (|| זרע נטע, ).
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning to cut down (trees);

occurrences.englishText: Though its root grows old in the earth,
A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse,
